Master Maven dependency management including dependency declaration, scope management, version resolution, BOMs, and dependency tree optimization.

```xml
</dependency>
```

```xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>

</dependency>
```

```xml
    <artifactId>jsr305</artifactId>
```

diagnosis.overall_diagnosis: The organizer hint points to defects/ambiguities in maven-build-lifecycle/SKILL.md around (1) toolchain selection and the agreed conventions for reproducing failures/build commands, and (2) how to handle dependency resolution and allowed modification scope for nested/invoker-style test projects. The current skill text is incomplete and does not define a concrete, correct reproduction workflow for this repo layout, nor does it clarify what can/should be changed in nested test projects versus the main modules, which can lead to wrong commands and edits during evaluation.

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: The file has an incomplete/underspecified 'Minimal diagnostic sequence' (only a cd command) and lacks explicit conventions for selecting the build toolchain (JDK/Maven settings) and for reproducing CI failures in /home/travis/build/failed/google/auto. It also does not document how to treat nested test projects (e.g., maven-invoker/it projects) in terms of dependency resolution, offline/local repo behavior, and what modification scope is acceptable (parent POM vs. nested project POMs), which the hint explicitly flags.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Update maven-build-lifecycle/SKILL.md to (a) explicitly state the required toolchain selection steps/assumptions (e.g., check java -version, mvn -version, enforce Maven Wrapper usage if present, avoid changing global toolchain unless required), (b) define a concrete, repo-relative failure reproduction contract (exact baseline commands to run first, how to rerun a single module/test, where logs/artifacts go, and how to handle multi-module builds), and (c) add a dedicated section on nested/invoker integration-test projects describing dependency resolution strategy (use of -pl/-am, -DskipITs toggles, local repo/relativePath, avoiding editing generated/target trees) and clearly define the allowed/expected modification scope: prefer fixing parent/module POMs and shared config; only edit nested test project POMs when the test itself is intended to validate that behavior, and document how to do so safely.
